title: Where in the Trajectory Does Monitor Suspicion Actually Localize?

original_idea.body:
# Where in the Trajectory Does Monitor Suspicion Actually Localize?

**Problem:** Risk: subtle agent sabotage evades step-level monitoring. The under-studied link is whether the monitor's suspicion concentrates ON the harmful step or smears diffusely, which would make step-level deferral useless even when whole-trajectory AUC looks fine.

**Direction:** Use SHADE-Arena transcripts, run an open monitor scoring each step, and for malign transcripts measure the rank of the true harmful step within the per-step suspicion ranking. Report localization accuracy vs mere global detection.

**Why it matters:** Many control protocols defer/edit at the step level, which only works if suspicion localizes correctly. A high whole-trajectory AUC can hide poor localization. Existing benchmark and monitor, no training.

**Relevant context:** SHADE-Arena (arXiv:2506.15740); Factor(U,T) (arXiv:2512.14745).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain with explicit links: poor step localization makes step-level deferral/editing useless despite good trajectory AUC.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run an open monitor per-step on SHADE-Arena and rank the known harmful step; inference plus stats, accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: localization accuracy (rank of true harmful step) vs global detection.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Existing open benchmark and monitor, no training; long-horizon agentic failure mode labs underweight.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over existing transcripts plus stats.

novelty.reasoning: Trajectory AUC reported; explicit step-localization measurement plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Monitoring AUC studied; localization angle plausibly open.
